verdict: Goldman Sachs grew revenue 14% to $17.2B and profit 19% to $5.6B as investment banking revenues jumped 48% from a year ago and trading stayed busy — a strong start built on Wall Street activity.

segments.name: Noninterest revenues
segments.note: Fees and trading: investment banking fees of $2.8B, FICC and equities trading, plus asset management fees.

segments.name: Net interest income
segments.note: Interest earned on loans and investments, minus interest paid — a smaller, steadier slice for Goldman than for retail banks.

flow.costPlain: Money set aside for loans expected to go bad — the closest thing a bank has to a cost of goods sold.

opex.name: Compensation and benefits
opex.note: Pay and bonuses — Goldman's biggest cost by far, rising with the firm's strong results.

opex.name: Transaction based
opex.note: Costs that rise and fall with trading and deal volume: brokerage, clearing and exchange fees.

opex.name: Communications and technology
opex.note: Trading systems, market data and communications.

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of offices, systems and equipment over their useful lives.

opex.name: Occupancy
opex.note: Rent and running costs for offices around the world.

opex.name: Other expenses
opex.note: Everything else that does not fit the lines above.

takeaways.title: Dealmaking woke up
takeaways.text: Investment banking revenues jumped 48% from a year ago to $2.8B — advisory fees of $1.5B led the way — as companies returned to buying, selling and raising money.

takeaways.title: EPS up 24%
takeaways.text: Diluted EPS rose 24% to $17.55 and return on equity was 19.8% — profit growth plus a shrinking share count from $5.0B of buybacks in the quarter.

takeaways.title: Client money keeps growing
takeaways.text: Assets under supervision reached $3.65T, with $87B of net inflows in the quarter — the wealth business gives Goldman steadier fee income between trading booms.

oneTimers: Platform Solutions revenue fell 33% to $411M as Goldman's exit from consumer banking winds down.
Preferred stock dividends of $227M sit between net earnings ($5,630M) and the $5,403M attributable to common shareholders.
